title: Benchmarking Document Parsers on Mathematical Formula Extraction from PDFs
abstract: arXiv:2512.09874v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Correctly parsing mathematical formulas from PDFs is critical for training large language models and building scientific knowledge bases from academic literature, yet existing benchmarks either exclude formulas entirely or lack semantically-aware evaluation metrics. We introduce a benchmarking framework centered on synthetically generated PDFs with precise LaTeX ground truth, enabling systematic control over layout, formulas, and content characteristics. For evaluation, we apply LLM-as-a-judge to assess semantic equivalence of parsed formulas, capturing mathematical meaning beyond surface-level notation differences. We validate this approach through a human study (250 formula pairs, 750 ratings from 30 evaluators), showing a Pearson correlation of r=0.78 with human judgment, compared to r=0.34 for character-level matching (CDM) and r~0 for text similarity. translated_title: 面向PDF数学公式提取的文档解析器基准测试
translated_abstract: 摘要：从PDF中正确解析数学公式对于训练大型语言模型和从学术文献构建科学知识库至关重要，然而现有基准要么完全排除公式，要么缺乏语义感知的评估指标。我们引入了一个基准测试框架，该框架基于合成生成的PDF，并带有精确的LaTeX真实标注，从而能够系统控制布局、公式和内容特征。在评估方面，我们采用“LLM作为裁判”来评估解析公式的语义等价性，捕捉超越表面符号差异的数学含义。我们通过一项人类研究（250对公式，来自30位评估者的750个评分）验证了该方法，结果显示与人类判断的皮尔逊相关系数为r=0.78，而字符级匹配（CDM）为r=0.34，文本相似度接近r~0。我们稳健的两阶段匹配流程结合了基于LLM的提取技术。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于合成PDF和LLM裁判评估的基准框架，用于语义感知地测试数学公式解析器，显著优于传统字符匹配方法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a benchmarking framework with synthetic PDFs and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation for semantically testing math formula parsers, significantly outperforming traditional character-level matching.
